get_place_details.description: Read the deepest view Nominatim has of a single place: every name variant, the tags behind it, the address hierarchy it sits in, the places it contains, and its search ranks. Name the place by its OpenStreetMap type and id, or by the 'place_id' from an earlier step.
get_place_details.display_str_template: Get everything OpenStreetMap holds about one place.
get_place_details.name: get_place_details

parameters.description: Which kind of object the id below refers to: a node is a single point such as a shop, a way is a line or an area such as a street or a building, and a relation is a group of objects such as a city boundary. Give this and the id, or give a place id instead.
parameters.name: osm_type

parameters.description: The object's numeric OpenStreetMap id, without the type letter.
parameters.name: osm_id

parameters.description: Nominatim's own id for the place, as returned by a search. Use this instead of the type and id above. Note that it is only valid on the server it came from.
parameters.name: place_id

parameters.description: Only needed when one OpenStreetMap object is indexed several times - a building that is also a tourist attraction, say. Give the tag key to choose between them, such as 'tourism'.
parameters.name: osm_class

parameters.description: List the addresses and points of interest that sit within this place. Can be a very long list for a city.
parameters.display_name: Include the places inside this one
parameters.name: hierarchy

parameters.description: Return the list above grouped by what each place is, rather than as one flat list.
parameters.name: group_hierarchy

parameters.description: Include the other OpenStreetMap objects that describe this same place, such as the city node linked to a city boundary. On by default.
parameters.name: linked_places

parameters.description: Include the words Nominatim indexed this place under. Useful for working out why a search did or didn't match it.
parameters.name: keywords

parameters.description: Return the place's outline as GeoJSON.
parameters.display_name: Include the shape of the place
parameters.name: include_geometry

parameters.description: Return the address split into its parts - house number, road, city, postcode, country - alongside the single-line version. On by default.
parameters.name: address_details

parameters.description: Return the mapped entrances to the place, each with its own coordinate. Useful for routing someone to a door rather than to the middle of a building.
parameters.name: entrances

parameters.description: Language for the returned place and country names. Defaults to English. A place with no name mapped in the chosen language comes back under its local name.
parameters.name: language

attribution.description: The OpenStreetMap attribution to display alongside these results

get_status.description: Check that the Nominatim server is up, and see how recently it pulled in edits from OpenStreetMap. Worth running first in a long workflow, and the quickest way to confirm your own Nominatim server is reachable.
get_status.name: get_status

data_updated.description: When the server last pulled in OpenStreetMap edits. A place mapped after this is not searchable yet.

healthy.description: True when the server is ready to answer queries

message.description: 'OK', or what is wrong with the server

status.description: Status code; 0 means everything is fine

list_broken_polygons.description: List the areas whose outline this server could not import cleanly - a boundary that doesn't close, or a shape that had to be simplified - each with the error that was recorded. How mappers find boundaries that need fixing, and how a self-hosted server's import is checked for damage.

list_deletable_places.description: List the places that have been deleted from OpenStreetMap but are still in this server's index, waiting for the deletion to be confirmed. A maintenance view, most useful for keeping an eye on your own Nominatim server.

lookup_places.description: Fetch up to 50 known OpenStreetMap objects by their ids in one call. Search results move as the map is edited, so a workflow that must keep pointing at the same place stores its id once and looks it up from then on. Every place this integration returns carries that id as 'osm_reference'.

This is the search box from openstreetmap.org.

description: Turn place names and addresses into coordinates, and coordinates back into addresses, using OpenStreetMap's own geocoder. Search the whole world map by text or by separate address fields, look places up by their OpenStreetMap id, and read everything the map holds about one of them. No account or API key required.
